title: Plague Still Exists and Cases Appear Every Year in Africa and the US
title_zh: 鼠疫从未消失，非洲和美国每年都有病例
lead: The plague, which once killed millions in Europe, has never disappeared. It is still found in some parts of Africa and the United States, but it can be treated with antibiotics.

paragraphs: The plague, a rare bacterial infection that famously killed tens of millions of people in 14th-century Europe, has never gone away. It is now easily treated with antibiotics, but cases still occur. Since the 1990s, most human cases have been reported in Africa, especially in Congo and Madagascar, according to the World Health Organization. In the United States, there are about seven human cases each year on average, mostly in rural areas of the American West, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention says.

Recently, a worker at a plague research institute in Siberia died of pneumonia. Unconfirmed media reports suggested she might have died of pneumonic plague, which raised alarm in Russia. Russian authorities said testing showed no evidence of plague, but the institute has been quarantined. "People think the plague is gone, it was something that occurred 500 years ago. It's not. It's here amongst us," said Simon Clarke of the University of Reading in the U.K. "Unless you get rid of those wild animals, which of course is not possible, then you're not going to get rid of the bacteria."

Pneumonic plague and the more well-known bubonic plague, also called the Black Death, are caused by the same bacteria, Yersinia pestis. The bacteria spread naturally among rodents like prairie dogs and rats. Fleas that jump from infected animals and bite people can spread the disease. Bubonic plague is the most common form. It causes painfully swollen lymph nodes, called buboes, most often in the groin, armpit and neck. Other symptoms include sudden high fever and chills, headaches, and pain in the abdomen, legs and arms, according to the Cleveland Clinic. There are two other forms: pneumonic plague, which infects the lungs and can be caused by inhaling the bacteria, and septicemic plague, an infection in the bloodstream. Both are fatal if not treated early, the WHO says. Bubonic plague often develops into the other two forms if untreated.

Besides flea bites, people can get plague by touching infected bodily fluids, so health experts recommend taking extra care when handling dead or sick animals. The plague can also spread through respiratory droplets from someone who has pneumonic plague. "If you cough, you can spread it to another person, but that doesn't travel very far," said Dr. Glenn Wortmann of MedStar Washington Hospital Center. "So you really need to be in face-to-face contact with that person to get pneumonic plague." That is why the chance of it spreading widely in Russia and then to the U.S. is very low, he said.

The plague was never eradicated, but we have become better at preventing its spread and treating it in humans. When treated early with antibiotics, the plague can be cured. The key is to see a doctor quickly—otherwise the plague can be deadly. There is a vaccine, but the WHO only recommends it for people at high risk of infection, such as laboratory and healthcare workers. There is not strong evidence that vaccines work against the pneumonic form. No plague vaccine is available in the U.S.
paragraphs_zh: 鼠疫是一种罕见的细菌感染，曾在14世纪的欧洲导致数千万人死亡，但它从未消失。如今鼠疫很容易用抗生素治疗，但病例仍时有发生。据世界卫生组织称，自20世纪90年代以来，大多数人类病例出现在非洲，尤其是刚果和马达加斯加。美国疾病控制与预防中心表示，美国平均每年约有7例人类病例，主要集中在美国西部的农村地区。

肺鼠疫和更广为人知的腺鼠疫（又称黑死病）由同一种细菌引起，即鼠疫耶尔森菌。这种细菌在土拨鼠和老鼠等啮齿动物中自然传播。跳蚤从受感染的动物身上跳到人身上叮咬，就能传播疾病。腺鼠疫是最常见的形式，会导致淋巴结疼痛肿胀，称为腹股沟淋巴结炎，最常见于腹股沟、腋窝和颈部。据克利夫兰诊所称，其他症状包括突发高烧和寒战、头痛以及腹部、腿部和手臂疼痛。另外还有两种形式：肺鼠疫感染肺部，可能因吸入细菌引起；败血型鼠疫是血液感染。世卫组织表示，两者若不及时治疗都会致命。腺鼠疫如果不治疗，往往会发展成另外两种形式。
除了跳蚤叮咬，人们也可能通过接触受感染的体液感染鼠疫，因此卫生专家建议处理死亡或生病动物时要格外小心。鼠疫还可以通过肺鼠疫患者的呼吸道飞沫传播。华盛顿医院中心的格伦·沃特曼博士说：“如果你咳嗽，你可以传染给另一个人，但传播距离不远。”“所以你真的需要与那个人面对面接触才会感染肺鼠疫。”他说，这就是为什么它在俄罗斯广泛传播并蔓延到美国的机会非常低。
鼠疫从未被根除，但我们在预防其传播和治疗人类病例方面做得更好了。如果及早用抗生素治疗，鼠疫可以治愈。关键是要尽快就医，否则鼠疫可能致命。有疫苗，但世卫组织只建议高风险感染人群接种，如实验室和医护人员。没有强有力的证据表明疫苗对肺鼠疫有效。美国没有鼠疫疫苗。
